chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Isa from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man who is one of my brothers has testimony (witnesses) with him, but not all of it is accepted by the judges among us. He said: 'When you know that it is true, then validate it in every way until his right is established.'
ai.seo_question: How to validate testimony when judges do not accept it all?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs that if a believer possesses evidence recognized as true but rejected by the standard judges (al-qudat), they must actively authenticate it through all valid means to secure their right. This highlights the Shia distinction between the authority of the Imams and the fallibility of contemporary judicial systems, emphasizing the believer's agency in ensuring justice is served despite institutional limitations.
